attribution_limitations: Figure 1 prints a quetiapine dose label that differs from the starting dose stated in the case text. The figure bar is not tied to a stated time point, so the source does not make them the same measurement. The text dose fact is kept as review_only; the image-printed value is recorded only in the visual record and is not used as a conflict side. Whether the difference reflects later titration is not stated.
The text says he refused neuroleptics, yet the same sentence says the family managed antipsychotics and confirmed he took them; both are recorded as written without reconciling.

"One week later, BMT was performed" opens a new paragraph and names no anchor, so the time anchor stays null and no interval is recorded. The test isolation is still ordered before BMT because the source states it was done to judge whether he could tolerate the BMT isolation phase, and the result was that he would be able to tolerate it. "Thirty days later" also opens a paragraph with no stated anchor and is not ordered.

The abstract reports follow-up at 2 and 4 years after BMT while the case text reports follow-up in 2017, 8 years after BMT; these are recorded as separate follow-up statements. The figure plots a course axis in months; plotted values are not extracted.

Discussion sentences about "this patient" (no infection during remission) are literal about the index patient; discussion sentences about animal studies and other reported patients are not patient facts.

The source says there was "not any description" of alcohol or drug use or epileptic seizures. This may report a negative history or only that nothing was recorded; it is not an explicit denial. The three items are kept absent but review_only and are left out of the summary.

claims.text: A 24-year-old man with an ordinary birth and normal growth, who worked in a corporation after university and had no family members with psychiatric or developmental disorders, developed insomnia, irritability and anxiety at age 23, followed by agitation, incoherent speech, persecutory delusions and paranoid ideation. Psychiatric assessment confirmed auditory hallucination, suspiciousness, social avoidance and social decline, and paranoid schizophrenia was diagnosed.
